standard.description: RF Reference Source (96000 Series; 96270A with microwave output, 96040A leveling head)
standard.confidence_text: [Not Specified] - not printed on the specification table
standard.reference: Fluke Calibration 96270A 27 GHz Low Phase Noise RF Reference Source, Technical Data, pub. 6002252B_EN (3/2020), p.6 "96270A summary specifications". The Operators Manual (chapters 1-3) prints no accuracy specification (p.1-2 refers to www.fluke.com).
standard.author: rows typed from the datasheet summary table (page image checked) by specs/build_96270a_standard_from_manual.py; operating limits read from the Operators Manual page images
standard.source_pdf: 96270A Technical Data 6002252B_EN.pdf (specification rows); 96270 Operator Manual.pdf (operating limits only)

notes.1: Manual p.1-2 (PDF p.8): "Complete specifications for the Product are at www.fluke.com." The Operators Manual prints no accuracy, flatness, stability, harmonic, spurious or 90 d / 1 yr / 2 yr specification. No confidence level / coverage factor is printed anywhere.
notes.2: Operating limits, NOT accuracy (Table 3-22, p.3-67, PDF p.93; Table 3-29, p.3-89, PDF p.115). Leveling Head output: frequency 0.001 Hz to 4.024 GHz, level -130.000 to +24 dBm (50 ohm) with 20 dBm max above 125.75 MHz and 14 dBm max above 1.4084 GHz; -136.000 to +18 dBm (75 ohm) with 14 dBm max above 125.75 MHz and 8 dBm max above 1.4084 GHz. Level units printed: dBm, Vp-p and Vrms (uV, mV, V), W (nW, uW, mW, W), dBuV. Level step 0.001 dB to 130 dB.
notes.3: Operating limits, NOT accuracy (Table 3-29, p.3-89, PDF p.115): 96270A Microwave O/P Direct: frequency 0.001 Hz to 27 GHz; level -4 dBm to +24 dBm, 20 dBm max above 1.4048 GHz, [-100 dBm minimum, above 20 GHz +18 dBm max] (the bracket is printed for the Extended Low Level Microwave Output option).
notes.4: Reference Frequency Output connector (Table 3-2, p.3-25, PDF p.51): BNC, 1 MHz or 10 MHz user selectable, 1.5 V pk-pk nominal into 50 ohm (-0.4 V to 1.1 V), 3.0 V pk-pk nominal into 1 kohm (-0.4 V to 2.6 V, TTL or 3 V compatible). No frequency accuracy or aging is printed.
notes.5: Reference Frequency Input connector (Table 3-3, p.3-25, PDF p.51): BNC, 1 MHz to 20 MHz in 1 MHz steps (phase-noise specification holds only for 10 MHz or 20 MHz), "Lock Range +/-0.3 ppm" (on-screen lock indicator), 1 V pk nominal (+/-5 V pk max), 50 ohm, lock bandwidth 0.5 Hz nominal. The lock range is the capture window of the external-reference input, not an output-frequency accuracy; it is not stored as a specification.
notes.6: SOURCE OF THE ROWS BELOW: Fluke Calibration 96270A 27 GHz Low Phase Noise RF Reference Source, Technical Data, pub. 6002252B_EN (3/2020), p.6 "96270A summary specifications" (rendered page image checked against the first transcription from a screenshot of the same table). Specified values are as printed; "typical" values are marked in the row label. The page says "Refer to the 96270A Extended Specifications for detailed specifications"; that document (confidence level, calibration period, 75 ohm head) was not supplied. Performance is specified at 23 degC +/- 5 degC (operating 0 to 50 degC, storage -20 to +70 degC).
notes.7: Printed on the same table, NOT accuracy and not stored as rows: Frequency / level range: Leveling Head O/P [50 ohm] 1 mHz to 4 GHz, -130 to +24 dBm to 125 MHz, +14 dBm at 4 GHz; Microwave O/P Direct 1 mHz to 27 GHz [with LL option], -4 [-100] to +24 dBm, above 1.4 GHz +20 dBm [above 20 GHz +18 dBm]; Microwave O/P with HF option 1 kHz to 27 GHz [with LL option], -10 [-35] to +18 dBm, above 1.4 GHz +14 dBm [above 20 GHz +12 dBm]. Resolution 10 uHz and 0.001 dB.
notes.8: Printed, not stored (limits that are not an uncertainty of the output): VSWR (Leveling Head O/P, 50 ohm): <= 1.05 to 100 MHz, <= 1.1 to 2 GHz, 1.0 + 0.05 x f(GHz) from 2 to 4 GHz; Microwave O/P direct <= 2.0 (typical), HF option splitter device <= 1.22. Harmonics <= 1 GHz: -60 dBc, > 1 GHz: -55 dBc; sub-harmonics <= 4 GHz: none, > 4 GHz: -60 dBc. Spurious >= 3 kHz offset: <= -84 dBc at 500 MHz, <= -78 dBc at 1 GHz, <= -66 dBc at 4 GHz, <= -48 dBc at 27 GHz. Phase noise at 1 GHz: -144 dBc/Hz typical, 10 kHz to 100 kHz offset.
notes.9: Printed, not stored: modulation AM, FM, PM internal/external to 4 GHz; frequency sweep 1 mHz to 4 GHz (Leveling Head) and 1 mHz to 27 GHz (Microwave O/P), linear or log; internal 300 MHz frequency counter; power meter readout for Rohde & Schwarz NRP-Z series thermal sensors (list cut off in the screenshot).

problems.what: Rows come from the SUMMARY specifications on p.6 of the Technical Data (3/2020), which refers to the 96270A Extended Specifications for detailed specifications. Check against the Extended Specifications (not supplied) before relying on them for an uncertainty budget; it should state the confidence level and calibration period.
Confidence level / coverage factor is not printed in the summary table. specmanager divisor() falls back to k = 2 for an unspecified level; set the divisor in the manager once known.
The summary table prints no calibration period. Every row is stored under "1 yr" only so the manager finds it; that is a placeholder, not a printed value.

Level accuracy is stored in dB as printed (kind OTHER, unit dB, 50 ohm). The uncertainty budget does not use kind OTHER, so nothing reads these rows yet; a dB-to-volts (or % of power) conversion convention must be decided before they feed a budget.

Printed: "+/-0.03 dB to 100 kHz, +/-0.05 dB to 128 MHz, +/-0.3 dB at 4 GHz". Stored as bands 0-100 kHz, 100 kHz-128 MHz and the single point 4 GHz; nothing is printed between 128 MHz and 4 GHz and the lower band edge of 0 Hz is assumed.
Printed levels "to -48 dBm / to -84 dBm / at -130 dBm" are kept in the label; the level bands are not split into numeric ranges because the table gives only the upper bound of each.
Printed: "Typically +/-0.5 dB to 4 GHz, +/-0.5 dB to 26.5 GHz". Typical values, not guaranteed, and the two lines are stored as printed (the two bands overlap).
Percent of power stored as a fraction of reading (1.06 % = 0.0106). The second set uses the printed assumption of a reference sensor with typical state-of-the-art uncertainty.

+/-0.05 ppm +/- 5 uHz stored for the full 1 mHz to 27 GHz; the table does not tie it to a period or to a temperature. Resolution 10 uHz taken from the table and stored on this row; the budget would add it as u(resolution) = 10 uHz / sqrt(12).
Printed "10 Hz to 128 MHz", relative to +10 dBm; at 110 dB the value is 0.15 dB. Stored as two rows by attenuation, not by a numeric amplitude range.
Level / frequency limits (notes 2, 3, 7), connector data (notes 4, 5) and the VSWR / harmonics / spurious / phase-noise data (note 8) are notes only; the schema has no field for them.
Confidence level is not specified on the sheet; set the coverage divisor in the manager before relying on this standard.
